question: Does floating the shared base orientation q_a (even constrained to its brightness isophote) lower the fast-seed ω-dir noise floor?
hypothesis: Freeing q_a so it can slide along its observed-brightness isophote sheds common-mode noise and lowers the fast-seed ω-dir floor.
narrative_md: Tested s089's shared-base hypothesis by floating q_a in the joint solve. On seed 119 it never beats pinning — at σ_q=2.5° pinned gives ω-dir 1.33°, free-unconstrained 4.41° (square system, overfits), brightness-isophote-constrained 2.24°. The isophote pins only 1 of q_a's 3 rotational DOF; the other 2 get spent fitting endpoint noise. Shared-base hypothesis refuted; the fast-seed floor is set by anchor quality, not solver freedom. Perturbed-truth anchors → not blind.
